Container.Name: pocket-dev
Container.Overview:
Browser-accessible terminal for Claude Code, mobile-first. Spawns a tmux session running Claude under a restart loop and exposes it via xterm.js over WebSocket, so a desktop or phone can attach to the same session and survive disconnects.
Click the WebUI button to open the terminal in your browser. Claude auto-starts; just begin typing.
Authentication: provide ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or run 'claude login' once. Auth persists in the config volume.

Config.Name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
Config.Description: Optional: Your Anthropic API key. If not provided, run 'claude login' in the terminal on first use.

Config.Name: Workspace
Config.Description: Directory where claude-code will work with your files

Config.Name: Claude JSON Config
Config.Description: Persists MCP server configs and settings across container restarts

Config.Name: Google Workspace Credentials
Config.Description: Persists Google Workspace OAuth credentials across container restarts

Config.Name: dgvpn State
Config.Description: Persists the Deepgram tailnet (dgvpn) registration across container restarts so you re-auth only when the ~24h key expires, not on every recreate.

Config.Name: Session State
Config.Description: Persists the list of open sessions and each one's Claude conversation id, so a container restart or update brings your tabs back and resumes the conversations instead of dropping you into one blank session. Without this mount, sessions survive a restart but not a recreate (an image update), because the state lives in the container's writable layer.

Config.Name: GitHub CLI Auth
Config.Description: Persists the 'gh auth login' token. Without it the token lives in the container's writable layer and vanishes on every image update, which breaks git push and gh part-way through a session.

Config.Name: flyctl State
Config.Description: Persists the flyctl install and its auth token across container recreates.

Config.Name: Tool Prefix
Config.Description: A writable prefix already on PATH (/opt/pd/bin) for CLIs a session installs for itself, so they survive container recreates. Use this rather than mounting /home/claude/.local, which would mask the claude and uv binaries baked into the image.

Config.Name: Docker Socket
Config.Description: Docker socket. WARNING: Mode=ro does NOT make the Docker API read-only. It marks the socket file read-only and nothing more; the daemon still accepts every write call (run, stop, rm) over it, verified on a live container. Anything in here can therefore start a privileged container and take over the host, so treat this mount as host root. Remove it, or put a filtered docker-socket-proxy in front of it, if that is not what you want.
